# Mortgage notes

Our loan on 14 Alder Street: 30-year fixed at 6.25%, closed with 10% down.

## Our loan at a glance

Principal and interest $2,215 a month. With escrow the payment is about $2,790. The loan servicer sends an annual statement each January. There is no prepayment penalty.

## Escrow account

The servicer collects one-twelfth of the yearly property tax and homeowners insurance bill with each payment and pays those bills for us. Once a year it checks the account: a shortage raises the monthly payment, a surplus over $50 is refunded.

## Private mortgage insurance

We put down less than 20%, so the lender adds private mortgage insurance (PMI) to the payment, about $140 a month. It protects the lender, not us. We can ask in writing to have it removed once the loan balance reaches 80% of the home's original value, if we are current on payments. The lender must cancel it automatically when the balance reaches 78% of the original value.

## Refinancing: when it pays off

Divide the closing costs by the monthly savings to get the break-even point in months. A refinance usually makes sense only if we will stay beyond that point, and a drop of about three-quarters of a point in the rate is a common rule of thumb. A new 30-year term restarts the clock on the interest.

## Extra principal payments

Adding $200 a month goes straight to principal and cuts years off the loan. Check that the servicer applies it to principal and not to next month's payment.

## Property tax appeals

If the assessed value looks too high, the county allows an appeal within 30 days of the assessment notice. Bring recent sales of similar houses.
